subject: physics_2
question_text: What is p-n junction diode? Define depletion region.

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. TRANSCRIPTION: the space before the question mark in the printed question is dropped. The book heads its second part 'Depletion layer'; the question asks for the depletion REGION and both names are used here, since they mean the same thing.

recall_prompt: Say what a p-n junction diode is, then say what the depletion region contains and why it forms.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: p-n junction diode
lines: p-n junction diode: when a p-type and an
junction is formed between them. This
single crystal, with one electrode on
each side, is called a p-n junction diode.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both semiconductor types, the junction, and the two electrodes.
steps.why: The two doped regions are not two separate crystals stuck together — they are two doped parts of one crystal, which is why charge carriers can cross the boundary at all.
common_mistakes: Saying two pieces are joined by a wire. The p and n regions are two parts of one crystal.
Leaving out the two electrodes. The question asks for a diode, which is a two-terminal device.

recall.must_convey: That joining a p-type and an n-type semiconductor forms a junction, and this with two electrodes is a p-n junction diode.
accept: p type and n type joined form a junction
one crystal with p side and n side
reject: narrow region with no free carriers

steps.memory_tip: Two doped regions, one crystal, two terminals — that is the whole device.

steps.label: Depletion region
lines: Depletion region: the narrow region on
either side of the junction which has no
free charge carriers. Holes and electrons
near the junction recombine and leave

lines.text: Depletion region: fixed ions, no carriers

steps.margin_note: Second mark. 'No free charge carriers' and 'immobile ions' are the two phrases the examiner looks for.
steps.why: The region is named for what has been removed from it. The mobile carriers have recombined and gone, so what remains is the fixed ionised impurity atoms — negative on the p side, positive on the n side — and their charge sets up the barrier field across the junction.
common_mistakes: Saying the region is empty. It holds fixed ions; it is empty only of MOBILE carriers.
Saying it lies on one side of the junction. It spreads on both sides.

recall.must_convey: That the depletion region is the narrow region on both sides of the junction with no free carriers, holding only immobile ions.
accept: narrow region on either side of the junction
reject: p type and n type joined together

steps.memory_tip: Depleted of what moves; left with what cannot move.

insider_note: Two definitions, one mark each. The second mark hangs on two phrases: no free charge carriers, and immobile ions.
